chapter: Russell and Armstrong years, Goodman and the road
title: Cuthbert, Georgia: Fletcher Henderson's home town
summary: The band visited Henderson's family in Cuthbert, where his father headed the school.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: But what were some of the little towns that were really rough like that? Can you think of any of the names?
No. It's kind of tough, you know, you just don't. One place was Fletcher Henderson's home. (His father was [mayor?] and everything else down there.)

Cuthbert, Georgia. Never heard of it until we were there, but one of my classmates, she always kept in touch. She said, you going with me. They ain't going to take me no place I can't take no chick. She had a brand new Ford. Walter Johnson drummer - we were in Fletcher Henderson's band together. He and I would always hang out together. ... They even killed a calf down there for us. It was nice. We stayed in his home for around about a week. Those people, they're very nice down there.
You say that Fletcher Henderson's father was the mayor of the town?
Yeah, he was boss of everything. Yeah, I'm not kidding.
He was the head of some school. I don't think I counted 10 white people while I was there.
Yeah. He was the principal of the school, just a little bit of everything. They had a beautiful home.
